source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 150,000.00 + wages (spouse) 100,000.00 = 250,000.00. Federal taxable income = 250,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 (31,500.00) = 218,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 250,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 250,000.00 + (0.00) = 250,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint) 8,240.00; line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 8,240.00 + 18,320.00 = 26,560.00; line 7 taxable income = 250,000.00 - 26,560.00 = 223,440.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 46,000.00 = 2,392.00 + 5.58% x (223,440.00 - 46,000.00 = 177,440.00) = 9,901.1520; total 12,293.1520 = 12,293.15. Line 7 is more than 100,000, so the form uses the Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34): 223,440.00 x 5.58% = 12,467.9520 less 175 = 12,292.9520, 0.20 less than the schedule because the printed subtraction is rounded; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 12,293.15. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 12,293.15.
accepted_approximations: Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
